title: How a Python Loop Works
summary: Master loops, ranges, and iteration in Python through clear visual code execution.

scenes.heading: A Loop Repeats Work
scenes.narration: A loop repeats an instruction for each item in a sequence, eliminating tedious repetitive code.

scenes.heading: Trace the Python Code
scenes.code:
for i in range(3):
    print(f"Processing item: {i}")
scenes.narration: The range function produces three consecutive values: zero, one, and two. The loop body executes once for each value.

scenes.heading: Visualizing Iterations
scenes.narration: During each pass, variable i updates to the next sequence number until all items are processed.

quizzes.question: What is the final value printed by for i in range(3)?
quizzes.explanation: range(3) produces 0, 1, and 2, so the final iteration prints 2.

quizzes.question: What is each pass through a loop called?
quizzes.explanation: A single cycle or execution of the loop body is called an iteration.

flashcards.back: One single pass of executing a loop's block of instructions.
flashcards.tip: Think of one lap around a track.

flashcards.back: Generates integer sequence from 0 up to n - 1.

title: How Neural Networks Learn
summary: Understand weights, forward propagation, and backpropagation in modern AI models.

scenes.heading: Neurons and Connections
scenes.narration: Artificial neural networks are inspired by biological brains, made of connected layers of mathematical neurons.

scenes.heading: Information Flow (Forward Pass)
scenes.narration: Raw inputs pass forward through layers where weights and activation functions transform them into predictions.

scenes.heading: Loss and Weight Updates
scenes.code:
error = loss(prediction, actual)
weights = weights - learning_rate * gradient
scenes.narration: When the prediction makes an error, gradients flow backwards to nudge weights in the direction of lower error.

quizzes.question: What algorithm calculates the error gradients to update weights?
quizzes.explanation: Backpropagation uses the chain rule of calculus to compute gradient of loss with respect to each weight.

quizzes.question: What does the learning rate control?
options: Step size taken when updating model weights
quizzes.explanation: The learning rate scales how large of a step the optimizer takes in the gradient direction.

flashcards.back: Passing input data through the network layers to calculate an output prediction.
A mathematical formula that measures the difference between model output and ground truth.

title: How the Internet & DNS Works
summary: From URL typing to IP resolution: learn how domain names turn into server connections.

scenes.heading: The Phonebook of the Web
scenes.narration: Computers find each other using IP addresses like 142.250.190.46, but humans prefer easy names like google.com.

scenes.heading: DNS Resolution Chain
scenes.narration: Your request asks DNS servers hierarchically until the authoritative server returns the exact destination IP address.

scenes.heading: Making the TCP/TLS Connection
scenes.code:
GET / HTTP/2
Host: example.com
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
scenes.narration: Once the IP address is known, your browser opens an encrypted TLS connection and requests the web page.

quizzes.question: What is the primary role of DNS?
options: To translate domain names into IP addresses
quizzes.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.

flashcards.back: The server responsible for tracking down the IP address on behalf of your computer.
The last segment of a domain name, such as .com, .org, or .edu.

title: Photosynthesis: Solar Power of Plants
summary: Discover how plants turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and clean oxygen.

scenes.heading: Nature's Solar Engine
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis converts solar energy into chemical energy stored in glucose, sustaining life on Earth.

scenes.heading: Input and Output Transformation
scenes.narration: Inside plant chloroplasts, green chlorophyll pigments capture photons to break water and fix carbon dioxide.

scenes.heading: The Light & Dark Reactions
scenes.narration: Light reactions produce ATP energy carriers; the Calvin cycle uses that energy to build sugars day and night.

quizzes.question: What green pigment absorbs sunlight inside plant chloroplasts?
quizzes.explanation: Chlorophyll is the pigment that absorbs blue and red wavelengths while reflecting green light.

quizzes.question: What crucial gas is released into the atmosphere as a byproduct?
quizzes.explanation: Plants split water molecules during light reactions, releasing oxygen gas into our atmosphere.

flashcards.back: The cellular organelle where photosynthesis takes place.
The light-independent stage that fixes atmospheric carbon dioxide into glucose.

title: Git & Version Control in 3 Minutes
summary: Working tree, staging area, commits, and branches explained with crystal visual diagrams.

scenes.heading: A Time Machine for Code
scenes.narration: Git tracks historical snapshots of your project, allowing you to branch, collaborate, and safely roll back.

scenes.heading: The Three Git States
scenes.narration: You edit files, stage desired changes with git add, commit them as permanent milestones, and push to share.

scenes.heading: Everyday Commands
scenes.code:
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Add interactive quiz feature"
git push origin main
scenes.narration: These four commands represent 90% of daily version control workflow.

quizzes.question: Which command stages modified files for the next commit?
quizzes.explanation: git add moves changed files from the working tree to the staging index.

flashcards.back: A permanent cryptographic snapshot of the repository at a specific point in time.
A lightweight movable pointer to a line of development.

title: Binary Search: Divide & Conquer
summary: Why O(log n) searches 1 billion items in just 30 steps.

scenes.heading: Cutting the Search in Half
scenes.narration: When a list is sorted, you never need to check items one by one. Check the middle and discard half every time!

scenes.heading: Halving the Search Space
scenes.narration: Each step cuts remaining candidates in half. Even for 4 billion elements, binary search finds the item in 32 comparisons.

scenes.heading: The Algorithm
scenes.code:
while low <= high:
    mid = (low + high) // 2
    if arr[mid] == target: return mid
    elif arr[mid] < target: low = mid + 1
    else: high = mid - 1
scenes.narration: Recalculate mid and adjust boundary pointers low or high.

quizzes.question: What prerequisite MUST be true before running binary search?
options: The list must contain only even numbers
The list must be stored in the cloud
The list length must be odd
quizzes.explanation: Binary search requires the data to be in sorted order to determine which half to discard.

quizzes.question: What is the time complexity of binary search?
quizzes.explanation: Because the space is halved at each step, time complexity is logarithmic: O(log n).

flashcards.back: Logarithmic time complexity; doubles of input size only add a single constant operation step.
